title: Gazpacho
subtitle: Chilled Spanish tomato and vegetable soup
excerpt: A silky, ice-cold blended soup of very ripe tomatoes, cucumber, red pepper, garlic, and good olive oil, seasoned with sherry vinegar. The soup of Andalucia, best on the hottest days.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gazpacho is a cold soup from the Andalucian region of southern Spain, where it has been eaten since at least the medieval period. The earliest versions were made from bread, water, olive oil, vinegar, and garlic: tomatoes were not added until the nineteenth century, after the tomato plant had spread from the Americas through Europe and become established in Spanish agriculture. Modern gazpacho is now defined by the tomato, supplemented with red pepper, cucumber, and onion. The dish is popular across southern Spain but is associated particularly with Seville, Cordoba, and Malaga. Sherry vinegar is the traditional acidulant of the Andalucian kitchen and gives a more complex, slightly woody flavour than wine vinegar. The soup must be made with very ripe, flavourful tomatoes: out-of-season or underripe tomatoes produce a pale, watery result without the characteristic red colour and deep tomato flavour.

content.text: Use the ripest, most flavourful tomatoes available: this soup cannot be rescued by technique if the tomatoes are poor. Leave the soup to chill for at least 4 hours before serving: a freshly blended gazpacho tastes raw and harsh; a chilled gazpacho tastes round and sweet. If blending produces a slightly coarse texture, pass the soup through a fine sieve for a completely smooth result. Serve in very cold bowls, straight from the fridge, with a drizzle of good olive oil on top.

items.preparation: good extra-virgin, plus extra to serve

content.text: Place all the vegetables, garlic, vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a blender. Blend on high for 2 to 3 minutes until completely smooth. Taste and adjust the seasoning and vinegar.
Pass through a fine sieve if you want a very smooth soup, pressing to extract all the liquid. Discard the solids. Chill for at least 4 hours, and up to 24 hours.
Stir before serving. Pour into chilled bowls. Drizzle with a little good olive oil and serve with a few small croutons or torn bread alongside if desired.
